To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cell-specific expression is associated with the transcription factors Sp 1 and Sp 3.
the transcription factors Sp3 and Sp1 are involved in the regulation of GIPR transcription in a cell type specific manner.
the transcription factors Sp-1 and Sp-3 bind to the rat GIPR promoter and are required for maximal GIPR gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of GIP and its receptor.
identifying the factors that regulate the expression of GIP receptors.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the Gipr gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Sp1/Sp3 transcriptional regulatory network is involved in the cell-specific expression of rat and human Gipr gene.
the transcription factors Sp3 and Sp1 are involved in the transcriptional regulation of the GIP receptor.
GIPR expression is cell specific and is regulated by Sp1/Sp3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GIPR is a cell-specific receptor and that the expression of the receptor is regulated by the transcription factors Sp 1/Sp 3.
Sp1 and Sp1/Sp3 are important for transcription of GIPR.
Sp1 and Sp2 are involved in the transcriptional regulation of the GIP receptor gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transcription factors Sp3 and Sp1 are critical for GIPR expression in pancreatic beta cells and that Sp1 binding sites in the GIPR proximal promoter region are critical for GDR expression in pancreatic beta-cells.
GIPR gene expression is regulated by the transcription factors, Sp1 and Sp2.
the GIP receptor gene promoter is regulated by the transcription factors Sp-1 and Sp-3, which may explain why this gene is expressed in some tissues and not in others.
